diagnostics.title: An effect has active audio and render inputs
diagnostics.explanation: An effect consumes existing audio through in or an isolated source render recipe through render_in. Both connections may be present when at least one is disabled.
diagnostics.wrongExample: eq tone { from drums.audio -> audio  from drums.render -> render }
diagnostics.rightExample: eq tone { from drums.audio -> audio  from drums.render -> render disabled }

diagnostics.title: Missing composition line
diagnostics.explanation: Every song starts with a composition line that names it and sets the tempo and the master seed. It can also say which AMPLE version the song was written for (ample 1).

diagnostics.title: Tempo out of range
diagnostics.explanation: The tempo must be between 20 and 300 beats per minute.

diagnostics.title: Malformed composition line
diagnostics.explanation: The composition line has a fixed shape: a quoted name, then in braces an optional AMPLE version (ample 1), the tempo and the master-seed.

diagnostics.title: Unknown module
diagnostics.explanation: features lists the opt-in modules: quality, credits, signing, secrets, lyrics, git-mirror.

diagnostics.title: Module value
diagnostics.explanation: A module is either on or off.

diagnostics.title: Assist level
diagnostics.explanation: assist is one of off, diff, button, auto.

diagnostics.title: Unknown lint rule
diagnostics.explanation: The lint line sets severities for rules that exist (see the Lint rules page).

diagnostics.title: Lint level
diagnostics.explanation: A rule level is off, info, warning or error.

diagnostics.title: Master seed out of range
diagnostics.explanation: The master seed must be an unsigned 64-bit whole number.

diagnostics.title: Unexpected text
diagnostics.explanation: A line must be a comment, the composition line, a features, lint or layout line, a block header ending with {, or inside a block.

diagnostics.title: Block not closed
diagnostics.explanation: Every block opened with { must be closed with } on its own line.

diagnostics.title: Bad block header
diagnostics.explanation: A block header has a type and a name: <type> <name> [pinned@<version>] [at ...] [flags] {

diagnostics.title: Bad pin
diagnostics.explanation: Only a pin may follow the name before the placement: pinned@<version>, with dotted numbers (major.minor for a built-in block).

diagnostics.title: Bad placement
diagnostics.explanation: Placement reads: at <bar> for <bars> [as <name>], several separated by commas.
diagnostics.rightExample: drums d at 3 for 8 as intro {

diagnostics.title: Unknown word in header
diagnostics.explanation: After the name, the pin and the placement only bake, lock, refresh, disabled and freeze seeds|plan are allowed before {.

diagnostics.title: Bar number or length
diagnostics.explanation: Bars start at 1 and a part is at least 1 bar long.

diagnostics.title: Bad from line
diagnostics.explanation: A connection reads: from <block>.<output> -> <input>.

diagnostics.title: Bad parameter line
diagnostics.explanation: A parameter is a name followed by its value.

diagnostics.title: Duplicate parameter
diagnostics.explanation: A parameter can be given once per block.

diagnostics.title: Bad use line
diagnostics.explanation: A module instance is written: use <module>[@version] as <name> {

diagnostics.title: Settings line
diagnostics.explanation: The settings line holds plugin settings of this song as pairs of plugin.name and a value, for example settings { acestep.synthModel sft }. Text with spaces goes in quotes.

diagnostics.title: View kept in comment lines
diagnostics.explanation: The groups, block sizes and pinned blocks of the canvas used to be kept in comment lines that start with # view. They belong in a view { } block, which is checked like the rest of the song. The quick fix writes the block; saving from the canvas does the same.

diagnostics.title: Scratch block of a rewind
diagnostics.explanation: The scratch block of a rewind block lists its events: at <time> { duration <time>; back <time> }. A time is seconds (6s), milliseconds (500ms) or decimal bars from the start of the block (4.5); back is how far the music jumps back after the scratch (negative: forward).

diagnostics.title: View block line
diagnostics.explanation: The view block keeps the canvas arrangement: group <id> { title, member, x, y, label lines }, size <block> <scale> and pin <block>. The song does not depend on it.

diagnostics.title: A proposal would widen the policy of the song
diagnostics.explanation: An assistant may only narrow the capabilities and limits of a song, never widen them. A proposal that would give the song a capability it did not have, or raise a limit, is not accepted. Widening is done by the owner, by hand.
diagnostics.wrongExample: A proposal that adds the capability network to the policy of the song.
diagnostics.rightExample: A proposal that only removes a capability or lowers a limit.

diagnostics.title: The parameter is driven by an expression
diagnostics.explanation: The parameter has an expression as its value, so a plain value cannot just replace it. Say what to do with the new value: override (keep the expression and use this value), bake (freeze what the expression gives), literal (drop the expression) or expression (edit the expression).
diagnostics.wrongExample: Setting block.cutoff to 800 Hz while cutoff is 600 + 3000 * traffic.level, without a mode.
diagnostics.rightExample: Setting block.cutoff to 800 Hz with the mode literal (the expression is dropped).

diagnostics.title: Doc comment names a parameter the helper does not have
diagnostics.explanation: A @param line of the doc comment of a helper must name one of its parameters. A parameter that was renamed or removed leaves its note behind, and the hover would show a note for something that is not there.

diagnostics.title: Doc comment says another type than the declaration
diagnostics.explanation: The type in a @param or @return line (also a union such as Interval|Int) is documentation, but it must say the same as the declaration; the type aliases of the file are written out first. A comment that promises more or less than the helper does is usually out of date.

diagnostics.title: Doc comment uses a type that does not exist
diagnostics.explanation: A type in a @param or @return line must be a type of the language (Int, Notes, Interval ...) or a type alias of the file. This is usually a typing mistake.

diagnostics.title: Call of a deprecated helper
diagnostics.explanation: The doc comment of the helper has an @deprecated tag. Every call of it is reported, so that the callers can move to what the comment points to.

diagnostics.title: Doc comment leaves a parameter out
diagnostics.explanation: The doc comment describes some parameters of the helper but not all. Add a @param line for the others, so that the hover says what each one means.

diagnostics.title: Block comment never closed
diagnostics.explanation: A comment that starts with /* runs until */. This one is never closed, so everything after it would be a comment. Close it with */, or use # for a comment that ends with the line. A /* inside a string, after a # or right after a letter or digit does not start a comment.

diagnostics.title: Old word for the song line
diagnostics.explanation: The first line of a song used to start with project. That word also names the folder of songs, so the line starts with composition now. Since v1 the old word is an error; the quick fix (or ample migrate) writes the new word.

diagnostics.title: No AMPLE version stated
diagnostics.explanation: The composition line can say which AMPLE version the song was written for (ample 1). Without it the song is read as the current version, so it could read differently after a future change. The quick fix adds the current version; nothing else changes.

diagnostics.title: Unknown AMPLE version
diagnostics.explanation: The ample number of a song must be a version this AMPLE reads. A higher number means the song was written for a newer AMPLE and cannot be built here; a song is never changed to a version by itself.

diagnostics.title: Bad meter
diagnostics.explanation: The meter on the composition line is written as top/bottom: the top number (beats) is 1 to 16 and the bottom number (the note that gets a beat) is 2, 4, 8 or 16. Without a meter a song is in 4/4.

diagnostics.title: Control expression not valid
diagnostics.explanation: A parameter that reads controls is written with numbers (with a unit), + - *, brackets and block.output. This one cannot be read.

diagnostics.title: Not a control
diagnostics.explanation: Only a control (the level of a follow block, a curve or a map) can steer a parameter. This output is audio or something else.

diagnostics.title: Wrong unit for a control
diagnostics.explanation: A control with a unit (control<Hz>, control<dB>) only steers a parameter in that unit, and a number in an expression must have the unit of the parameter. A control without a unit is scaled to the range of any parameter.

diagnostics.title: A parameter has two sources
diagnostics.explanation: A parameter is steered by a connection (from x.level -> cutoff) or by an expression (cutoff 600 + 3000 * x.level), not by both.

diagnostics.title: Unknown block type
diagnostics.explanation: The type must exist in the library (see Block types).

diagnostics.title: Duplicate block name
diagnostics.explanation: Block names are unique within the song.

diagnostics.title: Unknown parameter
diagnostics.explanation: A block only accepts the parameters of its type (listed in the hint).

diagnostics.title: No such block
diagnostics.explanation: A from line must name a block that exists in the song.

diagnostics.title: No such output
diagnostics.explanation: The named output does not exist on that block.

diagnostics.title: No such input
diagnostics.explanation: The named input does not exist on this block.

diagnostics.title: Type mismatch
diagnostics.explanation: Ports only connect when their types agree (audio to audio, midi to midi, text to text, data to data; any matches everything).

diagnostics.title: Input already connected
diagnostics.explanation: An input takes one source. Use a mixer to combine several.
diagnostics.wrongExample: two from lines to one input

diagnostics.title: Block reads itself
diagnostics.explanation: A block cannot be its own source.

diagnostics.title: Cycle
diagnostics.explanation: Blocks may not depend on each other in a loop; the path is shown in the message.
diagnostics.wrongExample: a reads b, b reads a

diagnostics.title: Bad seed value
diagnostics.explanation: A seed is the word derived or an unsigned 64-bit whole number from 0 to 18446744073709551615.

diagnostics.title: The chosen model cannot use this value
diagnostics.explanation: The song chooses a model that does not work with a value one of its blocks states. For a turbo model of the ACE-Step plugin that is a CFG guidance other than 1; the build refuses it. The editors mark the line and offer a quick fix that writes the value the model uses. Choose a Base or SFT model to use guidance above 1.
diagnostics.wrongExample: settings { acestep.backend server  acestep.synthModelFile acestep-v15-turbo-Q5_K_M.gguf }  ...  guidance 7

diagnostics.title: A song must state a required plugin setting
diagnostics.explanation: The song uses a plugin that wants every song to state some settings itself (for the ACE-Step plugin: acestep.backend, how the sound is made). The editors offer a quick fix that writes the project default into the settings line. Without it the block fails to build with AMP5370.

diagnostics.title: Invalid structured MIDI notes
diagnostics.explanation: A midi-clip notes parameter must contain valid bar:beat:length:pitch:velocity entries within the supported integer precision and one 4/4 bar.

diagnostics.title: The song does not exist
diagnostics.explanation: The command was given a song that is not in the project: the file is not there, or the path is wrong (a relative path is read from the project folder).

diagnostics.title: The score could not be converted
diagnostics.explanation: MuseScore did not finish converting the score within 2 minutes, or it could not convert the file to MusicXML (the first 500 characters of what it said are in the message).
diagnostics.wrongExample: A score file that MuseScore cannot open.
diagnostics.rightExample: A score file that MuseScore opens and exports.

diagnostics.title: The proposal is refused for good
diagnostics.explanation: The proposal would widen the policy of the song (capabilities or limits). That is refused and cannot be accepted later: capabilities and limits can only be widened by the owner, by hand.
diagnostics.wrongExample: Accepting a proposal that widens the policy of the song.
diagnostics.rightExample: Widening the policy by hand, in the policy of the song.

diagnostics.title: MIDI file unavailable or invalid
diagnostics.explanation: The MIDI block requires a project-owned, bounded Standard MIDI File that can be parsed safely.
diagnostics.rightExample: choose a valid .mid file inside the project

diagnostics.title: MIDI timing cannot be represented exactly
diagnostics.explanation: A note event falls between the supported six-decimal beat positions.
diagnostics.wrongExample: a note position not divisible into microbeats
diagnostics.rightExample: use MIDI note positions representable at six decimal places

diagnostics.title: MIDI track is unavailable
diagnostics.explanation: The selected track index does not exist in this MIDI file.
diagnostics.wrongExample: track 5 for a file with one track

diagnostics.title: MIDI module conversion cannot be completed
diagnostics.explanation: The generated module name, structure or supported size limits are invalid.
diagnostics.wrongExample: a module name containing a path separator
diagnostics.rightExample: a short path-safe module name such as midi-import

diagnostics.title: An autotune block without a method
diagnostics.explanation: Every autotune block states its method, because the sound depends on it a lot: spectral (a phase vocoder that keeps the formants, the default and usually the most natural) or psola (one pitch period at a time). The editors offer a quick fix that writes method spectral.

diagnostics.title: Invalid MIDI track selector
diagnostics.explanation: The midi block track parameter must be all or a nonnegative zero-based track index.

diagnostics.title: Unknown block tint
diagnostics.explanation: The tint parameter of any block colours its card and does not change the sound. It is one of red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple or pink.

diagnostics.title: Number outside the range of the parameter
diagnostics.explanation: A numeric parameter (or a point of an auto(...) curve) is outside the range its template declares. The build cuts it to the nearest limit without a word, so the sound is not what the number says.
diagnostics.wrongExample: gain 54 on a volume block (the range is -60 to +48 dB)
diagnostics.rightExample: gain 48, or two volume blocks in a row

diagnostics.title: Plugin not installed
diagnostics.explanation: The block needs an opt-in plugin that is not installed. AMPLE reports it instead of skipping the block.
diagnostics.rightExample: install the plugin, or remove the block

diagnostics.title: Part past bar 1024
diagnostics.explanation: Very long parts are probably a typo.

diagnostics.title: Regeneration is only guaranteed on this machine
diagnostics.explanation: Careful: regeneration is only guaranteed to give the same result on this machine with the same plugin, model and GPU setup. On another machine, driver or version it may sound different. Your current take is kept safe either way. See docs/regeneration.md.

diagnostics.title: Toolprint differs or determinism unverified
diagnostics.explanation: The toolprint of this machine differs from the one that made the take, or the plugin determinism is unverified, so a regeneration may not reproduce the take. Keep the stored take; regeneration verifies the result and defaults to restoring the previous take.

diagnostics.title: Path leaves the project
diagnostics.explanation: A project path must be relative and stay inside the project (or a registered link). Absolute paths and paths that climb out with .. are refused.

diagnostics.title: Invalid path or name
diagnostics.explanation: The path is empty, contains characters that are not allowed, has a name ending in a dot or a space, or uses a name that is reserved on Windows (CON, NUL, COM1 and so on).

diagnostics.title: Link leads outside the project
diagnostics.explanation: A folder or file inside the project is a symbolic link or junction whose target lies outside the project and outside every registered link.

diagnostics.title: Project is open elsewhere
diagnostics.explanation: Only one AMPLE instance may write to a project. The message says who holds the lock. Open the project read-only or close the other instance; a held lock is never broken automatically.

diagnostics.title: project.json is not valid
diagnostics.explanation: The project file is missing a field or is not valid JSON, so the project cannot be opened. Restore it from a backup or from .ample/backups.

diagnostics.title: Project made by a newer AMPLE
diagnostics.explanation: The project format version is newer than this AMPLE understands. Open the project with a newer AMPLE.

diagnostics.title: No migration available
diagnostics.explanation: The project uses an old format for which this AMPLE has no upgrade step.

diagnostics.title: Folder is already a project
diagnostics.explanation: A new project cannot be created in a folder that already has an .ample/project.json.

diagnostics.title: Project needs an upgrade
diagnostics.explanation: The project uses an older format. Opening it for writing upgrades it after making a backup copy of the old project file; a read-only open does not upgrade.

diagnostics.title: Not an AMPLE project
diagnostics.explanation: The folder has no .ample/project.json. A project is a folder with a mandatory .ample folder.

diagnostics.title: Project folder missing
diagnostics.explanation: A folder AMPLE expects inside .ample is missing. It can be created again; nothing is lost by that.

diagnostics.title: Unknown entry in .ample
diagnostics.explanation: There is a file or folder inside .ample that AMPLE does not create. It is left alone.

diagnostics.title: Leftover temporary file
diagnostics.explanation: A temporary file from an interrupted write was found. The real file is intact; the leftover can be deleted.

diagnostics.title: Project lock is held
diagnostics.explanation: Another AMPLE instance has the project open for writing. The heartbeat tells who and when it was last seen.

diagnostics.title: Old lock information
diagnostics.explanation: Nobody holds the project lock, but a heartbeat of an earlier holder remains. The lock is free to take.

diagnostics.title: Less free disk than the black box budget
diagnostics.explanation: The volume has less free space than the black box budget in the project settings. The journal may fill the disk before it is thinned.

diagnostics.title: A take needs a stored plan
diagnostics.explanation: The Always rule: a take can only be created after its plan is stored. The takebank refuses a take whose plan is not in the database, also when the database is used directly.

diagnostics.title: Data is not on disk
diagnostics.explanation: A stored blob listed by a take is missing. The take and its plan are still there: re-render the take from its plan (when the plugin is reproducible) or restore the data from a backup.

diagnostics.title: Unknown take, plan or data id
diagnostics.explanation: There is no take, plan or data with that id, an id prefix matches more than one, or the id is not of the form sha256: followed by 64 hex digits.

diagnostics.title: Plans and takes are immutable
diagnostics.explanation: Plans, takes and their data references are written once. They cannot be changed or deleted; dropping a take is a tombstone.

diagnostics.title: Plan is not valid
diagnostics.explanation: A plan has an unknown intent or schema, or its settings or toolprint are not valid JSON.

diagnostics.title: Black box could not be written
diagnostics.explanation: Every change is written to the black box journal before it is made. When the journal cannot be written (disk full, no access) the command is not run: the black box fails closed.

diagnostics.title: Nothing to restore
diagnostics.explanation: The black box record does not exist, is not a start record, or has no pre-image that fits inside the journal (very large files are only noted by size).

diagnostics.title: Dangerous act not accepted
diagnostics.explanation: A dangerous act needs the exact acceptance text typed by the user and a reason. Nothing was changed.

diagnostics.title: Data belongs to a take
diagnostics.explanation: A stored blob that a take uses is never removed by history cleanup. Takes are dropped with a tombstone, and their audio only through a separate dangerous act.

diagnostics.title: Tag is locked
diagnostics.explanation: A tag exists and is locked. Moving or removing it is a dangerous act: dry run, typed acceptance, reason and a tombstone.

diagnostics.title: Line name taken or protected
diagnostics.explanation: A line with that name already exists, or the line is studio (the real version), which cannot be dropped.

diagnostics.title: Line is dropped or in use
diagnostics.explanation: The line is dropped (restore it first), or it is the line you are working on and cannot be dropped (go to another line first).

diagnostics.title: Unknown line, tag or node
diagnostics.explanation: There is no line, tag or history node with that name, or a node prefix matches more than one.

diagnostics.title: History is immutable
diagnostics.explanation: History nodes are written once and are never changed or deleted. Cleanup only marks the content of unreachable nodes as reclaimed.

diagnostics.title: Cleanup plan is out of date
diagnostics.explanation: Something became reachable after the dry run, so the cleanup was refused. Run the dry run again.

diagnostics.title: Saved content is gone
diagnostics.explanation: A history clean-up removed the saved content of this version (it belonged to a dropped line), so it cannot be opened. Nothing in the project was changed.

diagnostics.title: Safety copy could not be written
diagnostics.explanation: Before a history clean-up removes the content of a dropped line it copies it to .ample/history-archive and reads the copy back. That failed (disk full or folder not writable), so the clean-up removed nothing.

diagnostics.title: Blocks form a cycle
diagnostics.explanation: The build engine found blocks that depend on each other in a loop, so there is no order in which to render them.

diagnostics.title: No renderer for this block
diagnostics.explanation: The block type has no renderer yet (AI voices and other plugin blocks need their plugin), or an input comes from a block that has no take. The block is skipped and the build goes on.

diagnostics.title: Could not mark the block as baked
diagnostics.explanation: The block was rendered but the song source could not be edited to add the bake flag (for example the block is not in the file).

diagnostics.title: Block implicitly disabled by a disabled source
diagnostics.explanation: A required input of this block comes from a block that is disabled, so this block has nothing to work on and is disabled with it. The build goes on without it. Optional inputs from a disabled block are simply left out.

diagnostics.title: This block is disabled
diagnostics.explanation: The block has the disabled flag, so it produces no take. Remove the flag to build it again.

diagnostics.title: An effect has no input to work on
diagnostics.explanation: An effect that accepts a render recipe has no audio input (in) or render input (render_in) connected, so there is nothing to process. The build leaves it out with this warning and renders everything else; connect an input, or remove the block.

diagnostics.title: A drum voice comes from the fallback kit
diagnostics.explanation: The kit does not have a sample for a voice used in the pattern, so the sample of the fallback kit plays instead. Add the voice to the kit, map it with the map parameter, or accept the fallback.

diagnostics.title: An automation expression cannot be read
diagnostics.explanation: A value that changes over the song is written auto(bar:value, bar:value, ...): whole bar numbers from 1, a colon and a whole number. The volume gain is in dB. A fade is written fadein(start, length, shape) or fadeout(start, length, shape): a start and a length in bars (5, 5.5) or seconds (12s, 1.5s), the shape lin, equal or exp, and it works on a volume gain and an effect mix only.

diagnostics.title: The project tempo differs from the tempo of a MIDI file
diagnostics.explanation: The notes of a MIDI file follow its own tempo, the bars of the song follow the project tempo. When they differ the notes slide against the bars and a note that goes on over a bar line is cut in two. Set the project tempo to the tempo of the file.

diagnostics.title: Seed is locked
diagnostics.explanation: Seeds are locked by default. Changing one probably makes reproduction of earlier takes impossible, so it needs an explicit unlock; every change is kept in the seed history.

diagnostics.title: Nothing to regenerate from
diagnostics.explanation: The block has no selected take (build it and select a take first), or a variant could not be made.

diagnostics.title: The selected take cannot be discarded
diagnostics.explanation: Select another take for the block first; the selected take is the one the song uses.

diagnostics.title: No such open decision
diagnostics.explanation: There is no open regeneration decision with that id (it was already answered), or the answer is not restore or keep-variant. Replacing the take needs the dangerous-act contract.

diagnostics.title: Plugin manifest is not valid
diagnostics.explanation: plugin.json is missing a required field or has a wrong value. The message lists every problem found.

diagnostics.title: Plugin protocol not supported
diagnostics.explanation: The plugin needs a newer plugin protocol than this AMPLE speaks, or it did not answer the handshake with protocol version 1.

diagnostics.title: Plugin output missing or outside its job folder
diagnostics.explanation: A plugin may only write inside its private job folder. It named an output outside it, named a file it did not write, or finished without any output.

diagnostics.title: Plugin sent invalid output
diagnostics.explanation: The plugin printed something to its output that is not a JSON-RPC message, so it was stopped.

diagnostics.title: Plugin output too large
diagnostics.explanation: A message or an output file was larger than the limit, so the plugin was stopped or its output refused.

diagnostics.title: Plugin crashed
diagnostics.explanation: The plugin process ended while a request was open. The render is recorded as a failed attempt; no take was made and the plan is kept.

diagnostics.title: Plugin timed out
diagnostics.explanation: The plugin did not answer within the time allowed and was stopped.

diagnostics.title: Plugin could not be started
diagnostics.explanation: The program named in the manifest could not be started, or the plugin does not support this operating system.

diagnostics.title: Plugin reported an error
diagnostics.explanation: The plugin answered a request with an error, for example a missing model. The message is the plugin's own.

diagnostics.title: Plugin settings are not valid
diagnostics.explanation: The settings do not match the settings schema of the plugin. The message lists what is wrong.

diagnostics.title: The document changed
diagnostics.explanation: The song was changed by someone else (another window or an edit in between) since you loaded it. Reload it and apply your change again.

diagnostics.title: No open dry run for this confirmation
diagnostics.explanation: A dangerous act can only be confirmed with the token of a dry run that is still open (one use, ten minutes). Start the act again.

diagnostics.title: Host not allowed
diagnostics.explanation: The server only answers requests addressed to localhost or 127.0.0.1. Use the address that ample serve printed, or start it with --allow-lan on a trusted network.

diagnostics.title: Origin refused
diagnostics.explanation: A web page from another address tried to call the local server. It is refused so that no other site can drive your project.

diagnostics.title: Session token missing or wrong
diagnostics.explanation: Every API call needs the session token that ample serve printed, in the header X-Ample-Token.

diagnostics.title: Request not valid
diagnostics.explanation: A field is missing or has the wrong type. The message names it.

diagnostics.title: Edit refused
diagnostics.explanation: The graph edit cannot be applied, for example an unknown block or a name that is already used. The message says why.

diagnostics.title: The song has errors
diagnostics.explanation: The song has errors and cannot be built. Fix the diagnostics first.

diagnostics.title: A plugin render takes long
diagnostics.explanation: A plugin block has been rendering for more than five minutes. This is only a notice in the log: the render goes on until the time limit (for ACE-Step the setting timeoutS, 900 seconds by default, at most 3600; the host adds a minute so the plugin's own message comes first).

diagnostics.title: A linked folder is not reachable
diagnostics.explanation: The folder of a linked catalog is not there (a drive that is not connected, a folder that was renamed or moved). Connect the drive, or relocate the link to the new place; no song needs to change.

diagnostics.title: Asset not found
diagnostics.explanation: The asset is not in the project, in its linked folders, in the user library or in the packs, or its file is gone from the folder. Link the folder that holds it, relocate, or restore the file.

diagnostics.title: Not the same catalog
diagnostics.explanation: The folder you pointed at does not carry the marker of that catalog, has another content fingerprint and does not hold most of its files. Check the folder, or relocate with force if you know it is the right one.

diagnostics.title: Read-only linked folder
diagnostics.explanation: A linked folder that is read-only is never written to (by AMPLE or by a plugin) and cannot be an output folder. Make the link read-write first, if you really want that.

diagnostics.title: Asset changed
diagnostics.explanation: The file is there but its content is not the one that was pinned in ample.lock. Accept the change (ample lock update) or restore the pinned file from the catalog or a backup.

diagnostics.title: Pack manifest not valid
diagnostics.explanation: pack.json is missing or has no name and version, or the name uses characters that are not allowed.

diagnostics.title: ample.lock is damaged
diagnostics.explanation: The lock file cannot be read, or there is none. It is written by ample lock update; do not edit it by hand.

diagnostics.title: --allow-all needs --login
diagnostics.explanation: Listening on every address with any host name is only allowed together with --login; otherwise the launch token would be the only protection.

diagnostics.title: Sign-in not set up
diagnostics.explanation: --login needs a stored user and password first: run ample auth set-password --user NAME.

diagnostics.title: Sign-in refused
diagnostics.explanation: Wrong user or password, or too many wrong attempts (locked for a minute).

diagnostics.title: Not enough room for the backup
diagnostics.explanation: The backup target has less free space than this backup needs. Nothing was written. Free space or choose another target.

diagnostics.title: Backup cannot be restored
diagnostics.explanation: The folder is not empty, or a stored file of the backup is missing or damaged (its hash is not the recorded one). A restore goes into a new folder, and nothing is overwritten with damaged data.

diagnostics.title: Archive not valid
diagnostics.explanation: The archive is not an AMPLE archive, has a format version this AMPLE does not read, is missing a file, or a file does not match its recorded hash. Nothing was imported.

diagnostics.title: Backup not found
diagnostics.explanation: There is no backup with that id in the target, or the start of the id matches several. Give more of the id (ample backup list).

diagnostics.title: SFZ region has no sample
diagnostics.explanation: An SFZ region did not name a sample and was skipped. Add a valid sample opcode to the region or remove the empty region.

diagnostics.title: Backup before the act failed
diagnostics.explanation: You asked for a backup before every dangerous act, and that backup failed, so the act did not run. Fix the backup target or turn the option off.

diagnostics.title: Invalid SFZ opcode value
diagnostics.explanation: An SFZ opcode value could not be interpreted and was ignored. Correct the reported opcode value in the SFZ mapping.

diagnostics.title: The file changed on disk
diagnostics.explanation: The file of an open song was changed outside the editor and the working copy changed the same place, so a save would overwrite one of the two. Nothing was saved. Look at the differences (GET /api/doc/disk) and choose per difference: the file's lines, the working copy's, both or your own text (POST /api/doc/resolve), then save again.

diagnostics.title: Encrypted data cannot be opened
diagnostics.explanation: The project (or a backup) is encrypted and the passphrase is missing or wrong, or a sealed record or file is damaged. Give the passphrase in AMPLE_PASSPHRASE. If it is lost, the recovery kit holds the key.

diagnostics.title: Vault or passphrase problem
diagnostics.explanation: The vault cannot be opened (wrong passphrase, damaged file, no vault yet) or a secret name or value is not acceptable. Passphrases and secret values are never taken from arguments.

diagnostics.title: Signature check failed
diagnostics.explanation: A signature does not match: the signed record or file was changed, the signature log was edited, records were cut off, or the signer is not the key you trust.

diagnostics.title: Signing key problem
diagnostics.explanation: There is no active signing key, the key file is damaged, or the passphrase does not open the private key. Make one with ample keys generate.

diagnostics.title: Encryption setting does not fit
diagnostics.explanation: Encryption is already on (or not on), or a backup folder holds backups sealed with another key. Use another folder for this project.

diagnostics.title: Module not found
diagnostics.explanation: The song uses a module that is not in the project (modules/), its linked folders or the installed packs. Link the folder that holds it or add the file.

diagnostics.title: Module version does not fit
diagnostics.explanation: The use asks for a version the module file does not satisfy: it needs the same major version and a minor version that is not older.

diagnostics.title: Unknown module parameter
diagnostics.explanation: The use sets a parameter the module does not declare.

diagnostics.title: Module input problem
diagnostics.explanation: The use connects an input the module does not have, or leaves an input of the module unconnected.

diagnostics.title: Unknown placeholder in a module
diagnostics.explanation: A value in the module uses $name but the module does not declare the parameter name.

diagnostics.title: Module has no such output
diagnostics.explanation: A block reads an output that the module instance does not offer, or the module points an output at a block that is not in it.

diagnostics.title: Module file is damaged
diagnostics.explanation: The module file lacks its module line or has a declaration (param, input, output) that cannot be read.

diagnostics.title: Modules loop or nest too deep
diagnostics.explanation: Module instances depend on each other in a loop, or are nested more than eight deep.

diagnostics.title: Module changed since it was pinned
diagnostics.explanation: ample.lock pins this module by hash and the file now has other content. Review it, then run ample lock update to accept it.

diagnostics.title: Quality rule failed
diagnostics.explanation: A take does not pass a quality rule (clipping, true peak, loudness, silence, DC offset, sample rate). Advisory: it never blocks saving unless the project policy requires the rule for a tag or promote.

diagnostics.title: Quality check could not run
diagnostics.explanation: The take has no audio, the audio is not 16-bit PCM WAV, or the quality policy file (.ample/quality.json) is damaged.

diagnostics.title: Credit or licence warning
diagnostics.explanation: A library asset in use has a licence that may not fit the project (for example non-commercial in a release), no licence at all, or the credits file is damaged. Advisory, not legal advice.

diagnostics.title: Quality policy stops this
diagnostics.explanation: The project policy requires rules to pass before a tag or a promote and the newest take of the master block does not pass them (or there is none). Fix the sound or change .ample/quality.json.

diagnostics.title: Analysis plugin needs permission
diagnostics.explanation: The analysis plugin wants the GPU or the network and was not allowed to. Nothing was started. Allow it on purpose (for example ample analyze --allow-gpu).

diagnostics.title: Unknown analyser
diagnostics.explanation: There is no analyser of that name. Run ample analyze --list.

diagnostics.title: Take cannot be analysed
diagnostics.explanation: The take has no audio, or its audio is not 16-bit PCM WAV, or no take was given.

diagnostics.title: Analysis result does not fit its schema
diagnostics.explanation: An analyser or plugin returned a result that breaks spec/schema/analysis-<kind>.schema.json, so it was not stored.

diagnostics.title: Analysis plugin problem
diagnostics.explanation: The plugin is not of kind analysis, does not offer that analysis, or did not answer the analyze request with a result.

diagnostics.title: Sample set problem
diagnostics.explanation: A drum kit or guitar block names a sample folder that is missing, holds no WAV files, lacks a file the pattern needs (for example tom.wav), or holds a file that cannot be played (only PCM or float WAV, one or two channels).

diagnostics.title: Pattern, strum or voicing not understood
diagnostics.explanation: A sample drum pattern is not a name or a list of voice:steps grids, a grid or strum holds characters that are not allowed, or the guitar voicing is not open, triad or power.

diagnostics.title: The server hit an unexpected error
diagnostics.explanation: Something failed inside the server that no rule foresaw. The message names the kind of error; the window that runs ample serve has the full details. If it repeats, write down what you did and report it.

diagnostics.title: A required plugin setting is missing in this song
diagnostics.explanation: A plugin marked a setting as required and this song has no value for it. Plugin settings belong to the song; the project-level settings are only the defaults for new songs. Use the quick fix to copy the project default into the song (the settings line), or set it in the plugin settings of this song.

diagnostics.title: Joined audio exceeds ten minutes
diagnostics.explanation: The joined inputs and gaps would produce more than ten minutes of audio. Shorten the inputs or reduce the number or length of gaps.

diagnostics.title: Unknown limiter option
diagnostics.explanation: This renderer accepts only the soft limiter or off. Choose one of those values for the limiter parameter.

diagnostics.title: Sequencer data cannot be used
diagnostics.explanation: The sequencer file, embedded sequence, lane assignment, channel data or referenced sample could not be read or used. Correct the reported field or provide a valid project file.

diagnostics.title: The local ACE-Step server is not available
diagnostics.explanation: A build needs the local ACE-Step server and no server answers on its port. AMPLE starts one itself when ace.exe and ace.models are set in the AMPLE settings.json (or in ACE_EXE and ACE_MODELS). Set them, or start the server yourself, or route the song to Faer.

diagnostics.title: The local ACE-Step server lacks a model file
diagnostics.explanation: A song names a model file (synthModelFile, lmModelFile, vocalExtractionModel or cliLmModel) that the local ACE-Step server does not list. The build stops before any work is done. Choose a file the server has (the plugin settings of the song list them), route the song to Faer, or add the file to the models folder.

diagnostics.title: The engine of a block is not valid
diagnostics.explanation: The engine parameter of an ace-music, ai-voice or voice-clone block is a place with an optional model: local, faer or faer-else-local, then a colon and a model family (default, turbo, sft, base, xl-turbo, xl-sft, xl-base) or a .gguf file name, for example faer:xl-sft. A voice-clone block takes only the place (it chooses its voice model with its own model parameter). The build stops before any work is done.

diagnostics.title: A reference recording needs the local ACE server
diagnostics.explanation: An ace-music or ai-voice block that takes a reference recording (audio on its reference input, or a voice_sample file) cannot be rendered on Faer: the Faer worker has no reference input yet. Set the block's engine to local, or remove the reference.

diagnostics.title: No blocks selected for the bundle
diagnostics.explanation: Choose at least one block before saving a bundle.

diagnostics.title: Bundle not found
diagnostics.explanation: The requested bundle is not present in the library. Check its name or add the bundle to the library first.

diagnostics.title: Invalid block name in bundle operation
diagnostics.explanation: A block name may contain only ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens.

diagnostics.title: Bundle conflicts with existing block versions
diagnostics.explanation: The project already contains different versions of one or more bundle blocks. Choose how to place or resolve those conflicts before continuing.

diagnostics.title: SFZ opcode not read
diagnostics.explanation: An .sfz sample set used an opcode this version does not read yet, or a <region> could not be built (no sample, or no key/lokey/pitch_keycenter). The opcode's value is kept in the file and not applied; the region is skipped if it could not be built at all. See docs/samples.md "SFZ sets" for what is read today.

diagnostics.title: Autotune settings
diagnostics.explanation: The key of an autotune block is auto, chromatic, or a root and a scale (A minor, F# major, D dorian). Its fixes are written as <start>-<end> <note>, separated by ;, optionally followed by vibrato <percent>, or off to leave that part alone. A time is seconds (6s), milliseconds (500ms) or decimal bars from the start of the block (4.5).

diagnostics.title: Chop pattern or slices
diagnostics.explanation: The pattern of a chop block holds slice numbers from 1 to the number of slices, rests (-) and repeats like 3*2, and a list of slice starts must be seconds that rise and lie inside the sound.
diagnostics.wrongExample: chop words { pattern "1 2 9"  from voice.audio -> audio }
diagnostics.rightExample: chop words { pattern "1 2 3 3*2 -"  from voice.audio -> audio }

diagnostics.title: Vocoder inputs
diagnostics.explanation: A vocoder needs a voice on its modulator input and a sound on its carrier input, and both must have the same sample rate.
diagnostics.rightExample: vocoder talk { from voice.audio -> modulator  from chord.audio -> carrier }

diagnostics.title: Rewind events
diagnostics.explanation: The events of a rewind block are written as: at <time> scratch <length> back <length>, separated by ;. A time is seconds (6s), milliseconds (500ms) or decimal bars from the start of the block (4.5). A rewind block with sound fx needs a sample on its fx input.

diagnostics.title: SFZ file problem
diagnostics.explanation: An .sfz sample set is missing, cannot be parsed (a bad #include, an unclosed header), references a sample or #include that does not exist or that lies outside the SFZ file's own folder, or defines no usable (pitched) region.

diagnostics.title: Duplicate path in package
diagnostics.explanation: A package cannot contain multiple entries with the same project-relative path. Create a package with unique paths.

diagnostics.title: Package is incomplete
diagnostics.explanation: The .ampletx data ended before the complete package was read. Recreate or copy the package again.

diagnostics.title: Package format is newer than this AMPLE version
diagnostics.explanation: This package uses a format version newer than this AMPLE can read. Open it with a compatible newer AMPLE version.

diagnostics.title: Package file failed its integrity check
diagnostics.explanation: A file's size or SHA-256 does not match the package manifest, so the package may be damaged. Obtain a valid copy of the package.

diagnostics.title: Save the song before exporting a package
diagnostics.explanation: Package export uses the saved song. Save the song and retry the export.

diagnostics.title: Song has no master output to export
diagnostics.explanation: Add or connect a master block to define the final output before exporting.

diagnostics.title: Final output has blocks that failed to build
diagnostics.explanation: Every block in the requested final output must build successfully before the song can be exported. Resolve the reported build failures and retry.

diagnostics.title: Derived export boundary has no audio
diagnostics.explanation: The selected boundary does not provide renderable audio and cannot be used to create a derived song.

diagnostics.title: Resolve derived export conflicts first
diagnostics.explanation: The derived export has conflicts that must be reviewed and resolved before the package can be created.

diagnostics.title: Export package already exists
diagnostics.explanation: An existing package is never overwritten. Choose a different package path.

diagnostics.title: Package not found at the selected path
diagnostics.explanation: No package exists at the selected path. Choose an existing .ampletx package.

diagnostics.title: Package has no master preview
diagnostics.explanation: This package does not include a master preview that can be imported as audio.

diagnostics.title: Import destination is not an AMPLE project
diagnostics.explanation: Choose an existing AMPLE project folder as the package import destination.

diagnostics.title: Package cannot be imported in this environment
diagnostics.explanation: The package has one or more compatibility differences that prevent import in this environment. Review the reported differences and use a compatible environment or package.

diagnostics.title: Package import would overwrite different project content
diagnostics.explanation: The destination already contains different content at a package path. Use the conversion flow or import into a new project.

diagnostics.title: Codex identity is not allowed by this server
diagnostics.explanation: This server does not permit the selected Codex identity and does not silently replace it. Choose an allowed identity or ask the administrator to change the server policy.

diagnostics.title: Acknowledge AI agent risks first
diagnostics.explanation: Starting an AI coding agent requires explicit acknowledgement of its risks before the task can begin.

diagnostics.title: Project Codex identity is not linked
diagnostics.explanation: Link a Codex identity to this project in project settings before starting a Codex task.

diagnostics.title: Codex executable not found
diagnostics.explanation: Install Codex or configure its executable path so AMPLE can start it.

diagnostics.title: Codex request failed
diagnostics.explanation: The Codex request failed. Review the reported error and retry the task when the underlying problem is resolved.

diagnostics.title: Assistant proposal is still being checked
diagnostics.explanation: Wait for proposal validation to finish, or explicitly accept it anyway if that is appropriate.

diagnostics.title: Project changed while Codex was working
diagnostics.explanation: The proposal is based on project files that changed during the task. Rebase or review the proposal against the current project before accepting it.

diagnostics.title: Unknown or expired assistant task token
diagnostics.explanation: An assistant tool received a task token that is not active or no longer belongs to a running task. Start or resume the intended task and use the token it provides.

diagnostics.title: Server setting cannot be widened through the API
diagnostics.explanation: A project may turn off capabilities, but it cannot widen server policy or select the Codex program. Ask the administrator to change those settings.

diagnostics.title: Assistant edit request is invalid or ambiguous
diagnostics.explanation: The requested file edit could not be applied safely because its operation is incomplete, its target is missing, or its match is ambiguous. Read the file again and provide a more precise edit, including an occurrence when needed.

diagnostics.title: FFmpeg is required for FLAC output
diagnostics.explanation: Install FFmpeg or set AMPLE_FFMPEG to its executable path before exporting FLAC audio.

diagnostics.title: Proposal could not be measured
diagnostics.explanation: AMPLE could not prepare the proposal for measurement. Review the reported error and retry after resolving the setup problem.

diagnostics.title: Proposal needs offered audio files
diagnostics.explanation: The proposal refers to audio files offered to the assistant. Include those files in the proposal or revise it so the song does not depend on unavailable audio.

diagnostics.title: Koda is busy
diagnostics.explanation: Koda does one thing at a time. A second question while the first one is still being worked on is refused; stop the first one or wait for it.

diagnostics.title: File exceeds the 60 MB limit
diagnostics.explanation: This operation accepts files up to 60 MB. Choose a smaller file.

diagnostics.title: MIDI to audio converter has no input
diagnostics.explanation: Connect a MIDI sequence or MIDI notes to the converter before building it.

diagnostics.title: Effect preview range is invalid or too long
diagnostics.explanation: Choose a non-negative preview interval no longer than 30 seconds.

diagnostics.title: Not enough free disk space to store a take
diagnostics.explanation: The drive that holds the takebank is full, or has less free space than the render needs. Free space on the drive, clean up takes in the Storage panel (ample storage clean), or move the takebank to another drive (ample storage move).

diagnostics.title: The takebank cannot be written
diagnostics.explanation: A take could not be stored: the folder is read-only, the file is in use or the drive is not reachable. Check the data folder of the project (.ample/data or the configured data path).

diagnostics.title: Clean-up refused
diagnostics.explanation: The clean-up was not run: it needs the exact acceptance text, or the plan changed since the dry run. Run the dry run again and accept it.

diagnostics.title: The take data folder is not reachable
diagnostics.explanation: The configured data path of the takebank is not there (an unplugged drive, a renamed folder). Connect the drive or change the data path; builds render again what is missing.

diagnostics.title: Not enough disk space for this build
diagnostics.explanation: The estimate of this build is larger than the free space of the drive that holds the takebank. Free space, clean up takes, move the takebank, or build a smaller part.

diagnostics.title: Unknown final
diagnostics.explanation: The song has no final with that name. List the finals of the song and use one of them.

diagnostics.title: The clean-up cannot tell what is protected
diagnostics.explanation: A source, a history revision, a working file or the storage options could not be read, so the clean-up cannot be sure which takes are in use. Nothing was removed. Close the file, repair it and run the dry run again.

diagnostics.title: A place that can never be written
diagnostics.explanation: The assistant asked to write somewhere that is never open (the project own .ample folder or a system folder), or the path is not a full path. Remarks go to ample_findings inside the project.

diagnostics.title: No permission to write there
diagnostics.explanation: The assistant tried ample_write_outside without a permission for that path. It asks first with ample_request_access; the person decides.

diagnostics.title: Note pipeline syntax
diagnostics.explanation: The notes of a midi-clip are written as a pipeline, but the text is not valid: a bracket is not closed, an operator has no arguments, or a step is missing.

diagnostics.title: Unknown note operator
diagnostics.explanation: A pipeline step names an operator that does not exist. The message suggests the nearest one and the editors offer to replace it.

diagnostics.title: Note operator argument
diagnostics.explanation: An operator got an argument it cannot use: a wrong number of arguments, a wrong kind, a missing or wrong unit.

diagnostics.title: Range is reversed
diagnostics.explanation: The end of a range is before its start.

diagnostics.title: Fractional bar position
diagnostics.explanation: A bar position with a fraction is allowed (1.5 is the middle of bar 1), but it is often a slip; there is no automatic fix.

diagnostics.title: Notes before the beginning
diagnostics.explanation: A shift moved notes before the start of the value; they are dropped.

diagnostics.title: Unknown note source
diagnostics.explanation: A pipeline reads the notes of a block that does not exist or has no notes to read (only a midi-clip with notes can be read).

diagnostics.title: Note sources read each other
diagnostics.explanation: Two clips read each other through their note pipelines, so neither can be worked out.
diagnostics.wrongExample: notes b.notes   (in a)  and  notes a.notes   (in b)

diagnostics.title: Stale note bake
diagnostics.explanation: What a bake stage is made of has changed since it was baked (the pipeline before it, a clip it reads, or the tempo). The build keeps using the stored notes; bake again or detach the stage.
diagnostics.wrongExample: a bake stage whose input-hash no longer matches

diagnostics.title: Baked notes were edited by hand
diagnostics.explanation: The notes stored in a bake stage no longer match their notes-hash: they were edited by hand. With strict on the stage this is an error. Bake again to go back, or accept the change.
diagnostics.wrongExample: a bake stage whose notes were edited
diagnostics.rightExample: bake the stage again, or accept the edit

diagnostics.title: Bake file cannot be read
diagnostics.explanation: A bake stage keeps its notes in a file of the project, and that file is missing or cannot be read.

diagnostics.title: Bake stage has no notes yet
diagnostics.explanation: A bake stage without notes does nothing yet. Bake it to store the notes of the pipeline up to that point.

diagnostics.title: Length auto needs valid notes
diagnostics.explanation: A part written as "for auto" takes the length of the notes of the clip; while the notes have problems the length is taken as one bar.
diagnostics.wrongExample: at 1 for auto  (notes with an error)

diagnostics.title: Note pipeline too large
diagnostics.explanation: A note pipeline made more notes than the limit allows. Make the pipeline smaller; a project may raise its own limit up to the limit of the server.
diagnostics.wrongExample: a pipeline that merges a clip with itself many times

diagnostics.title: Note pipeline may be too large
diagnostics.explanation: Worked out without running it, the pipeline can make more notes than the limit allows (a repeat multiplies, a concat adds). Make it smaller, or raise the limit of the song with settings { notes.maxEvents 500000 }; the limit of the server (2000000) cannot be passed.

diagnostics.title: Wrong seed
diagnostics.explanation: A seed is a whole number, stable("name"), or one of those followed by .fork("label") (a name in quotes or a whole number). Anything else, or a stable(...) without exactly one name, is refused.

diagnostics.title: random-seed() has not been picked
diagnostics.explanation: random-seed() asks AMPLE to choose a seed from OS randomness once. Until a number has been written into the song the result could not be reproduced, so the pipeline refuses to build; the fix picks the number and writes it into the song.

diagnostics.title: Random-stream problem
diagnostics.explanation: A random-stream has to be declared in the clip (random-stream name seed) before name.next() is read; a stream is not a seed, a plain seed has no next(), and a name may be declared only once per clip.

diagnostics.title: Stable name looks like a typo
diagnostics.explanation: A stable name used only once that is within two edits of a name used elsewhere starts a new random family and silently changes the music. The fix uses the name that is used more often.

diagnostics.title: Same seed used twice
diagnostics.explanation: The same seed used twice by the same operator in one clip gives identical random offsets, so the two results are correlated. Give the second its own fork if they should differ.

diagnostics.title: Random-stream never read
diagnostics.explanation: A random-stream was declared in the clip but its next() is never called.
diagnostics.rightExample: remove the line, or read it with drift.next()

diagnostics.title: Argument of the wrong type
diagnostics.explanation: An argument is not a value of the type the operator expects: a pitch class (C, C#, Db ... B), a scale (minor, dorian ...), a count, an octave, a velocity, a pitch, a probability or a chord symbol. The catalogue (spec/note-ops.json) says what each argument is.

diagnostics.title: Quoted word
diagnostics.explanation: A pitch class, scale or mode is a bare word, not a string. A quoted word of the right vocabulary is still understood; the fix removes the quotes.

diagnostics.title: Missing unit
diagnostics.explanation: A duration needs a unit (bar, beat, tick, ms or s): a bare number does not say what it counts, and the choice changes the music, so no unit is chosen for you.

diagnostics.title: Reserved
diagnostics.explanation: Reserved: a bare number in an Interval slot (transpose(+7)) means semitones and is accepted silently; this code is not used.

diagnostics.title: Fractional interval
diagnostics.explanation: An interval that is not a whole number of semitones (50cents) is a valid Interval, but note events carry whole pitches only (microtonal pitch bend is not supported by this operator yet).

diagnostics.title: Fixed span differs from the notes
diagnostics.explanation: A block says for N, but the only notes that feed it have a statically known or derived span of another length. The fix writes for auto, so the block follows the notes.
diagnostics.wrongExample: gm play at 1 for 4 { from melody.notes -> notes }   (melody is 2 bars)
diagnostics.rightExample: gm play at 1 for auto { from melody.notes -> notes }

diagnostics.title: Not a whole number
diagnostics.explanation: A count, octave, velocity or pitch is a whole number. The fix offers the value rounded half to even; Floor, Ceil or Truncate change the music differently and are your choice.

diagnostics.title: Unit of the wrong kind
diagnostics.explanation: A unit does not belong to the type that is expected: pitch distances use st, oct or cents; lengths use bar, beat or tick; times use ms or s.

diagnostics.title: Lossy number conversion
diagnostics.explanation: A decimal number that is not whole cannot become a whole number by itself: rounding is a musical choice. Say how with Round, Floor, Ceil or Truncate (the fix offers Round, which rounds half to even). A whole decimal such as 4.0 is accepted.

diagnostics.title: Conversion failed
diagnostics.explanation: Int(x) and Float(x) only convert what is exactly representable; Round, Floor, Ceil and Truncate say how a decimal becomes a whole number.

diagnostics.title: emit and return mixed
diagnostics.explanation: emit builds Notes (each emit merges into the result): a helper uses emit, or return with a value, not both, and an emitting helper returns Notes.
diagnostics.wrongExample: helper h(Notes n) -> Notes { emit n  return n }
diagnostics.rightExample: helper h(Notes n) -> Notes { emit n }

diagnostics.title: Stable name shared by every call
diagnostics.explanation: A stable name inside a helper is the same namespace on every call, so two calls draw the same random numbers. Pass the seed in as a RandomSource parameter and fork it per call.
diagnostics.wrongExample: helper soft(Notes n) -> Notes { n |> thin(0.5, seed=stable("hat")) }
diagnostics.rightExample: helper soft(Notes n, RandomSource seed) -> Notes { n |> thin(0.5, seed=seed) }

diagnostics.title: While loop reached its max
diagnostics.explanation: A while loop always has a max. Reaching it with the condition still true is an error (a silently truncated result changes the music); write max N stop when stopping there is intended.

diagnostics.title: Code after return
diagnostics.explanation: The statements after a return in the same block are never run.

diagnostics.title: Helper uses a dynamic value but is not declared dynamic
diagnostics.explanation: A helper that reads the clock, OS randomness or the environment, or calls a dynamic helper, must say so: dynamic helper. The word is a permission, the effect itself is always inferred, so a missing mark can never make a song look reproducible. The fix marks the helper.

diagnostics.title: Unknown helper or operator
diagnostics.explanation: There is no helper, operator or built-in with this name. The fix offers the nearest name.

diagnostics.title: Helper name with other casing
diagnostics.explanation: Names are compared ignoring case, so the call works, but it is written differently from its declaration. The fix writes the declared spelling.

diagnostics.title: Name declared twice
diagnostics.explanation: Two declarations have the same name (names are compared ignoring case), or a helper has the name of a built-in.

diagnostics.title: Recursive helper without a return type
diagnostics.explanation: A helper that calls itself must say what it returns (-> Type): the types of a recursion cannot be inferred.

diagnostics.title: Unknown type
diagnostics.explanation: A parameter or return type is not a type. The fix offers the nearest type.

diagnostics.title: Variable misuse
diagnostics.explanation: A variable that was made with let cannot be changed (use var), a name must be defined before it is assigned, a name is defined once per block, a constant cannot be defined in terms of itself, and a division by zero has no value.

diagnostics.title: Stale value bake
diagnostics.explanation: A baked value (bake expression as value @hash) no longer matches what its expression is made of: a helper, a block or the tempo changed. The fix bakes it again.

diagnostics.title: Baked value overridden on purpose
diagnostics.explanation: A baked value with override keeps its own number while the expression resolves to something else; the message says what the expression gives now.

diagnostics.title: Limit above the cap of the server
diagnostics.explanation: A song may lower a limit or raise it up to the cap of the server, never above it; the cap is used.

diagnostics.title: Baked value changed by hand
diagnostics.explanation: The number of a baked value was changed while the hash still matches the expression: write override to keep it on purpose, or bake it again.

diagnostics.title: The clip cannot be baked
diagnostics.explanation: Baking turns the notes of a clip into plain notes. It needs a clip that has notes, notes that are a pipeline (not plain text), and an editable piece with the number that was asked.
diagnostics.wrongExample: bake on a clip without notes, or on notes that are not a pipeline, or on piece 9 of a clip that has 2 pieces.
diagnostics.rightExample: notes clip.notes |> bake name, on a clip that has a pipeline.

diagnostics.title: Loop limit
diagnostics.explanation: A loop would run more often than limits.loop-iterations allows (the song can raise it up to the cap of the server).

diagnostics.title: Fuel exhausted
diagnostics.explanation: Helper code used more evaluation steps than limits.fuel allows. Fuel is counted in abstract steps, so every evaluator stops at the same place.
diagnostics.rightExample: a smaller loop, or settings { limits.fuel N }

diagnostics.title: Stack depth
diagnostics.explanation: Helpers call each other deeper than limits.stack-depth allows.
diagnostics.rightExample: a recursion with a base case

diagnostics.title: Name is not defined
diagnostics.explanation: A word in a helper that is not a parameter, a variable, a constant or a word of the language (a scale, a pitch class, true, false, a member of a type) is a symbol, and that is rarely meant: a misspelled name, or a variable used before it is declared. In arithmetic it is an error. This is found in every branch, also in the ones that never run.

diagnostics.title: A path without a value
diagnostics.explanation: A helper that says what it returns can end without a value on some path (an if without an else, a loop at the end): calling it then fails. Every path ends with return VALUE or an expression.

diagnostics.title: Unused variable
diagnostics.explanation: A variable made with let or var in a helper is never read.

diagnostics.title: A statement that does nothing
diagnostics.explanation: A statement that is only a name, a number or a calculation, and is not the last one of its block, has no effect: its value is thrown away.

diagnostics.title: Helper never called
diagnostics.explanation: A helper of a song that no clip, property or other helper calls. Silence it with # ample-ignore AMP2086 on the line above when it is meant to stay.
diagnostics.wrongExample: helper old(Int p) -> Int { return p }

diagnostics.title: Helper not available
diagnostics.explanation: A call of a helper whose declaration has a syntax error. The error is on the declaration; the calls follow when it is fixed (this note replaces a second, confusing unknown-operator error).
diagnostics.wrongExample:
helper f(Int p) -> Int { retrun 1 }
notes ... f(1)

diagnostics.title: The kit has no sample for this voice
diagnostics.explanation: A pattern of a drums block asks for a voice (kick, snare, tom ...) that the sample folder of its kit has no WAV file for. When the block is built that is AMP5350 and the block fails, and so does everything that needs it. This check looks at the folder before anything is rendered. Use a voice the kit has, map the voice to a sample of another kit (map tom=other-kit/tom) or give the block a fallback kit that has it.

diagnostics.title: The music that feeds this block is longer than the block
diagnostics.explanation: A block that has no length of its own (no at ... for ... and no bars) covers 8 bars. When the notes or the MIDI that feed it are longer, everything after bar 8 is cut off: it is not rendered and not heard. Give the block a length, or write for auto so that it follows the music that feeds it.

diagnostics.title: Memory limit
diagnostics.explanation: The notes made by helper code together take more memory than limits.memory allows (an estimate of 64 bytes per note, counted at every pipeline result and helper result, so every evaluator stops at the same place).
diagnostics.wrongExample: repeating a long clip thousands of times
diagnostics.rightExample: a shorter result, or settings { limits.memory 256 } (never above the cap of the server)

diagnostics.title: Property depends on a volatile value
diagnostics.explanation: A block property expression reads the clock, OS randomness, the environment or a dynamic helper: its value can differ between builds, and the song is not reproducible (status dynamic) until the value is baked: property bake expression as value.

diagnostics.title: A name with hyphens that was meant as a subtraction
diagnostics.explanation: A hyphen belongs to a name (canon-voice), so a-b is one name. When every part of it is a variable, a constant or a number the author most likely meant a subtraction: write spaces around the minus.

diagnostics.title: Not available
diagnostics.explanation: environment() is not part of the language: reading the environment of the machine would put its secrets into songs and takes. A capability-based replacement may come later.

diagnostics.title: Capability setting
diagnostics.explanation: A capabilities.<name> setting names a capability that does not exist, has a value other than on or off, switches on a capability that the server or the project forbids, or switches on a capability that was turned off earlier (an explicit off is permanent and the capability stays off).
diagnostics.wrongExample:
settings { capabilities.environment off }
settings { capabilities.environment on }

diagnostics.title: Capability denied
diagnostics.explanation: The code reads the clock, OS randomness or the environment (or, later, the network, files, processes or plugins) while that capability is off: by default, by the server, by the project or by this song. The message says which.
diagnostics.wrongExample: environment("AMPLE_KEY")   (capability environment is off by default)

diagnostics.title: Helper name
diagnostics.explanation: Helpers and functions are written in lowerCamelCase (canonVoice); blocks and resources keep their kebab-case. Rename the helper with F2 so every call follows.

diagnostics.title: Old spelling
diagnostics.explanation: random-seed() is spelled randomSeed() (helpers, functions and built-ins are lowerCamelCase). The old spelling still works for now.

diagnostics.title: Component declaration cannot be read
diagnostics.explanation: A component is declared as component <name> version <x.y.z> { ... } with input, output, property, process, ui, requires, deprecated, migrate and seal lines inside. This line or block does not follow that form.

diagnostics.title: Name used twice in a component
diagnostics.explanation: Inputs and properties are the parameters of the process, so they share one list of names, and a name may not be a word of the component language.

diagnostics.title: Type a component cannot use
diagnostics.explanation: The ports and properties of a component use the types of the musical type model (Notes, Int, Float, Bool, Duration, Interval, Percent, ...) and List or Range of those. There are no types of its own for components.

diagnostics.title: Component changed since it was pinned
diagnostics.explanation: ample.lock pins the semantic hash of every component a song uses. The component has another hash now, so the song may sound different. Review it, then accept the change (the editor offers it) or run ample lock update.

diagnostics.title: Default of a property does not fit
diagnostics.explanation: A property needs a default that is a value of its type and inside its range (only a Notes property may start empty).

diagnostics.title: Unknown attribute
diagnostics.explanation: Only the built-in attributes exist: MinValue, MaxValue, Step, Options, Editor, DisplayName, Description, Category, Experimental and KodaFact. Attributes of your own are not allowed.

diagnostics.title: Attribute not valid here
diagnostics.explanation: An attribute says where it may stand and on which types: MinValue, MaxValue and Step go on ordered types (Int, Float, Percent, Duration ...), Options on a String, Editor on Notes. A type that already says it is better than an attribute.

diagnostics.title: Attribute arguments wrong
diagnostics.explanation: An attribute takes a fixed number of arguments of one kind (a number, a text in quotes or a name), MinValue may not be above MaxValue and Step must be more than 0.

diagnostics.title: Component without output or process
diagnostics.explanation: A component has one output and a process that says what it makes.

diagnostics.title: Component takes a native name
diagnostics.explanation: The names of the native block types are reserved: a component never shadows one. Give it a namespace.

diagnostics.title: Seal does not match
diagnostics.explanation: The component was changed after it was sealed. A sealed version is immutable, so the seal is void: the component counts as unsealed. Make a new version (unseal, change the version, seal again).

diagnostics.title: Component is not sealed
diagnostics.explanation: An unsealed component is a development object: it builds, but nothing about it is trusted and its results are always worked out again. Seal a version to make it immutable.

diagnostics.title: Same component and version with another content
diagnostics.explanation: Two files declare the same canonical id and version with a different sealed content. That is a hard conflict: one of them is a different component that must have another id or version.

diagnostics.title: Same name for different components
diagnostics.explanation: Two different components (different canonical ids) are exported under the same path. Remap one with import ... as or give it another path.

diagnostics.title: More than one current version
diagnostics.explanation: At most one version of a component is marked current: it is the default over a higher release.

diagnostics.title: No version matches
diagnostics.explanation: The instance asks for a version (stable@1.8, stable@^2) that no declaration of the component has.

diagnostics.title: Import cannot be read
diagnostics.explanation: An import names a file that cannot be found or read.

diagnostics.title: Reexport cannot be made
diagnostics.explanation: A reexport names a symbol that does not exist, or reexports in a circle.

diagnostics.title: Instance does not fit its component
diagnostics.explanation: The properties of an instance must have the type of the property, stay inside its range, and the inputs that are not optional must be connected.

diagnostics.title: Not supported in this version
diagnostics.explanation: A component has Notes ports and one output in this version; other port types and several outputs are reserved for later.

diagnostics.title: Component version is deprecated
diagnostics.explanation: The version an instance uses is deprecated: the author says what to use instead, and may offer an automatic migration.

diagnostics.title: Deprecation or migration cannot be read
diagnostics.explanation: A migration is written migrate <from> -> <to> { ... } with an impact (none, equivalent, musicalChange or destructive) and statements that rename, copy, set, drop or relink.

diagnostics.title: Migration available
diagnostics.explanation: The version of this instance has an automatic migration to a newer one. Nothing is changed until you preview and accept it.

diagnostics.title: Version cannot be read
diagnostics.explanation: A version is major.minor.patch, with an optional pre-release (4.0.0-beta.1); a request may start with ^ or ~ and may leave out minor and patch.

diagnostics.title: Canonical id not valid
diagnostics.explanation: A canonical id is lower-case letters, digits, dots and hyphens with at least one dot (com.koda.effects.canon-maker). It is required before a component is sealed and exported.

diagnostics.title: Attributes without a declaration
diagnostics.explanation: Attributes are only read directly above a component declaration (or inside a component above a port or property).

diagnostics.title: Fallback of an input is not notes
diagnostics.explanation: The fallback of an input is a property of type Notes of the same component: the notes that stand in when nothing is connected.

diagnostics.title: Capability not declared
diagnostics.explanation: A component says which capabilities it needs (requires clock). A process that reads the clock, OS randomness or the environment without saying so is refused; the policy of the song and the server decides whether it may.

diagnostics.title: UI names something that does not exist
diagnostics.explanation: The declarative ui of a component binds to properties and ports of that component.

diagnostics.title: Audio component contract not valid
diagnostics.explanation: A component that has Audio ports makes audio: Notes may go in (an instrument turns them into sound) but a Notes output next to Audio ports is not offered, and an Audio input has no fallback.

diagnostics.title: Unknown name in an audio process
diagnostics.explanation: A name in the process must be an input, or a let defined before it is used. Names are read top to bottom, so an audio graph can never loop back on itself.

diagnostics.title: Wrong type in an audio process
diagnostics.explanation: A processor takes Audio and gives Audio, and each argument has the unit of its parameter (a time for time, a Percent for a percentage, a Gain for dB, a frequency for Hz). Notes cannot go into an audio processor and the other way round.

diagnostics.title: Audio graph too big or without output
diagnostics.explanation: An audio component has at most 64 processor nodes and 8 outputs, and every output must be given by an emit.

diagnostics.title: Unknown audio processor
diagnostics.explanation: The name is not a processor (an effect block with an audio in and an audio out, gain, pan or mix). A Notes operation cannot be used on Audio.

diagnostics.title: Unknown processor argument
diagnostics.explanation: The argument is not a parameter of that processor. The hover of the processor lists them.

diagnostics.title: Audio graph limit or note
diagnostics.explanation: A note about an audio graph that does not stop the build: a processor without client preview, or a block that declares a delay (latency). The branches of one component are lined up inside it; to line the component up with the other tracks of the song too, write settings { audio.latencyCompensation on } (see AMP2250).

diagnostics.title: Unknown word in the layout
diagnostics.explanation: A word of the ui block that is not a widget, a container or preview. The message lists the words.

diagnostics.title: The layout names something that is not there
diagnostics.explanation: A widget names a property (or, for a meter, an output) that the component does not have. A near name is suggested.

diagnostics.title: The widget does not fit the type
diagnostics.explanation: A knob, slider or xy needs a number property, a toggle a Bool, a choice a property with Options, a jam a Notes property. Use field for any type.

diagnostics.title: The layout is too big
diagnostics.explanation: A layout has at most 64 items and containers nest at most four deep.

diagnostics.title: The same property twice in the layout
diagnostics.explanation: Two widgets edit the same value. Keep one, or make the second a readout.

diagnostics.title: A live preview that cannot be
diagnostics.explanation: A live preview is for audio components: the sound changes while a knob moves. A Notes component is not played while a knob moves.

diagnostics.title: Not a colour
diagnostics.explanation: A tint (in a ui block or as #[Tint(...)]) is a colour name (accent, green, yellow, orange, red, pink, purple, blue, teal, gray) or a text such as "#ff8800".

diagnostics.title: Components call each other in a circle
diagnostics.explanation: A component never calls itself, directly or through other components: when A calls B and B calls A there is no end. Notes components call each other like a function (emit koda.notes.up(source, semitones=7)), audio components call each other as a processor (audio |> koda.fx.dreamEcho(feedback=20%)). The message names the circle (A -> B -> A). Break it by moving what both need into a third component that neither of them calls back.

diagnostics.title: A call of a component does not fit
diagnostics.explanation: When a Notes component calls another Notes component, the first unnamed value is its first input and everything else is given by name: the other inputs and the properties (a property left out takes its default). This is reported for a name that the called component does not have, for a value that is not an input and for an input that is not given.

diagnostics.title: A call names no version
diagnostics.explanation: A component that calls another component without a version gets the default version of it (the one marked current). When the called component gets a newer default, the caller makes something else, and a caller that is not sealed does not notice. Write the version in the call, koda.notes.up@2.0.0(source) (or @2.0, @^2.0), to keep the one you tested. A sealed component records what it calls in its hash and breaks its seal instead, so this is only said for components that are not sealed.

diagnostics.title: Latency compensation is on
diagnostics.explanation: The song says settings { audio.latencyCompensation on }, so AMPLE put a shift block in front of every input of a mixer, bus, send or vocoder that arrives earlier than the latest input, and a cut block in front of the master that takes the remaining delay off the start. Only blocks whose template declares a latency (latencyMs) count; no built-in block does today, because the renderers look ahead over a whole file without delaying it. The setting is off by default: a song without it keeps its plan ids.

diagnostics.title: --bind needs an IP address
diagnostics.explanation: The address after --bind must be an IP address such as 127.0.0.1 or ::1, not a host name. Behind a reverse proxy on the same machine use 127.0.0.1 together with --allow-all, so only the proxy can reach the port.

diagnostics.title: Build parallelism out of range
diagnostics.explanation: A project may ask for fewer blocks rendered at the same time than the server allows (1 up to the limit of the server, which is at most the number of cores), or null to follow the server. More than the server allows is refused.
